To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two-level construction of the n- gram index, which is equivalent to the relational normalization of the n-grams, is an effective way to reduce the size of the index and to improve the query performance, especially when the database size is large.

the structural optimization of the (full-text, error-tolerant) n-gram inverted list significantly reduces the size, and improves the query processing time, compared with the original n-gram index; and the query performance is similar to or slightly better than that of Makinen’s CSA.

the proposed n-gram/ 2L index significantly reduces the size of the (full-text n-gram) index and improves the performance of queries, especially for short query lengths, by using the relational optimization theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
structural optimization of the (full-text n-)gram index using relational normalizations.
the efficient construction and maintenance of large text databases, which has become an important issue for the Web and for the digital library.
the n-grams that are used for approximate string matching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in terms of size reduction and query processing time, the n- gram/2L index performs better than the CSA in most cases.
the n- gram/2L index can be used for a short query length and the CSA can be used for the other cases.
the n- gram/2L index performs best when the query length falls in the middle range, and that it performs worst when the query length gets too long.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for short queries, the n- gram/2L index would be better than the CSA, and for long queries the CSA would be better than or similar to the n-gram /2L index.
, in terms of both the size and the performance, the n- gram/2L index can be considered as a better alternative to the CSA for full-text n- gram indexing.
the n- gram/2L index can be a good candidate for a full-text index for a large-scale text database.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relational normalization process is useful not only for relational databases but also for full-text databases.
the relational normalization process is useful not only for relational data but also for non-relational data such as text data, and that it is a promising approach to optimize the index structure.
the structural optimization of an n-gram index is a very promising approach for large full-text databases.
